key_insight: Sequential thermal evaporation produces different solid-state conversion routes in wide-bandgap and narrow-bandgap perovskite stacks, so bandgap control must be tailored to each absorber chemistry.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical design rule for building solvent-free, evaporated all-perovskite tandem solar cells with tunable bandgaps and improved device performance.
method: Time-sliced ex situ analysis of sequentially evaporated precursor stacks
Comparison of WBG and NBG solid-state conversion pathways during annealing
Fabrication and testing of evaporated all-perovskite tandem devices
evidence_signal: The study reports bandgaps from 1.26 to 1.96 eV, a first evaporated all-perovskite tandem efficiency of 19.2%, and 80% average efficiency retention after 1,200 h at 65 °C.
watch_item: Vertical compositional gradients and incomplete interdiffusion in narrow-bandgap stacks may complicate reproducibility and long-term stability.
paper_title: Divergent Solid-state Conversion Pathways in Evaporated All-perovskite Tandem Solar Cells
